acceptance.given: An adversarial target case is supplied to the Toolchain evaluation selector.

oracle.expected: The evaluation emits a rejection outcome and no success verdict for the adversarial target case.
forbidden: Treating the adversarial target case as successful.
oracle.observable: The case-specific evaluation verdict emitted by the Toolchain runtime.

acceptance.then: The adversarial target case is rejected.
acceptance.when: The evaluation selector executes the adversarial target case.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute an adversarial target case that would be incorrectly reported as success unless the rejection behavior is implemented.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make the Toolchain case-evidence evaluation reject success for an adversarial target case.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persistent-state or schema migration; reverting restores prior verdict classification behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: Adversarial target presented -> evaluation rejection recorded.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selector observes a rejection for the adversarial target case and observes no success verdict.

acceptance.given: Six materially distinct Matrix Cases have been selected for Toolchain execution.

oracle.expected: The case-evidence record maps every Matrix Case to a distinct fixture and distinguishable execution state.
forbidden: Two materially distinct Matrix Cases use the same fixture or indistinguishable execution state.
Fixture or state is changed so that case distinction is removed during execution.
oracle.observable: The case-to-fixture and case-to-state assignments checked by the Toolchain case-evidence selector.

acceptance.then: Each of the six Matrix Cases is executed with distinct fixture and state.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain prepares and executes the six Matrix Cases.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Supply two materially distinct Matrix Cases with shared fixture or indistinguishable state and require the case-evidence selector to reject the mapping.

affected_subjects: Fixture and state distinctness for Matrix Case executions
slice_hint.behavior_change: Require Toolchain case-evidence validation to preserve distinct fixture and execution-state assignments for all six materially distinct Matrix Cases.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persistent-state or schema migration; reverting restores prior Matrix Case evidence validation.

slice_hint.state_transition: Six identified Matrix Cases without established distinct assignments -> six executions with distinct fixture/state assignments.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selector verifies six case-specific fixture/state assignments and rejects any shared or indistinguishable assignment between materially distinct cases.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain external process is configured for execution under a time budget.

oracle.expected: The process completes within its configured finite bound or is terminated at that bound with an unsuccessful terminal outcome.
forbidden: The external process runs without a finite time bound.
oracle.observable: The runtime stage result and process-execution receipt, evaluated during external-process execution.

acceptance.then: The process completes or terminates within the finite time bound.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain runtime executes an external process.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run an external process whose execution exceeds its configured bound and require an unsuccessful bounded timeout result with no fabricated case observation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a finite execution time bound for every Toolchain external process and make budget exhaustion unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persistent-state or schema migration; reverting restores prior process-stage timeout handling.

slice_hint.state_transition: External process executing under a time budget -> completed within bound or terminated unsuccessfully at the bound.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The runtime selector observes either bounded completion or bounded unsuccessful termination; it never observes an unbounded process.

acceptance.given: A replay has unexplained drift in an input that determines its result.

oracle.expected: The Toolchain marks the replay result stale or terminates replay through a fail-closed outcome.
forbidden: The result remains treated as current or valid despite unexplained result-determining input drift.
Replay proceeds as valid without stale classification or closed failure.
oracle.observable: The replay freshness classification and terminal replay decision, evaluated before a current result can be accepted.

acceptance.then: The result is stale or replay has failed closed.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain detects unexplained drift in a result-determining replay input.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate a result-determining replay input without an explained binding update and require the freshness selector to reject a current or valid replay result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Classify unexplained result-determining replay-input drift as stale or fail closed before the replay result can be accepted as current.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persistent-state or schema migration; reverting restores prior replay-freshness handling.

slice_hint.state_transition: Replay with unexplained result-determining input drift -> stale result or fail-closed replay.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selector observes stale classification or fail-closed termination and never accepts the drifted replay as current or valid.
